summary: Daemon exposes remote-controlled PTY and command execution on installer host
details: The package installs a long-running agent daemon that connects out to a hardcoded first-party WebSocket endpoint (default wss://api.ai-support-agent.com/ws/agent-terminal) and pipes incoming 'stdin' frames, after base64 decoding, directly into a node-pty PTY spawned on the installer's host, and accepts tmux list/kill/split-window and PTY resize/close control from the same channel. A second control path subscribes to an AppSync notification channel and, on AGENT_COMMAND messages, fetches a payload from the API and dispatches it through a local executeCommand() that supports execute_command (shell exec), ssh_exec, server_setup_exec (Ansible over SSH), file_read/file_write/file_delete/file_mkdir, process_list/process_kill, reboot, and update. The daemon is installed as a persistent per-user service via systemd user units, macOS LaunchAgents with RunAtLoad+KeepAlive, and Windows scheduled tasks, so the remote-to-shell path auto-reconnects across reboots. Any party operating the control server, or with authenticated access to it, can execute arbitrary shell commands, read/write arbitrary files, kill processes, SSH into other hosts, and reboot every machine running the daemon. This is a network-to-shell backdoor regardless of the service's advertised purpose or its first-party endpoint.
